title: Grateful Dead Live at Monterey Performing Arts Center on 1969-06-14
lineage: SBD > MCass > Cass > DAT > ZA2 > SF > CD > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A solid soundboard capture of a wildly energetic 1969 show, highlighted by a smoking Eleven, twin Lovelights and an epic Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The recording (sound‑board) is clear enough to enjoy the night’s fire‑storm performance – a blistering Eleve​n, two soaring Lovelight sandwiches and a spacey Dark Star that keep the energy at peak.  While the mix isn’t pristine (a bit muddy in places and a tiny drop‑out on St. Stephen), the band’s playing is consistently tight and charged, making this one of the era’s must‑hear shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly praise the musical performance (especially The Eleven, Lovelight and Dark Star) with high energy; recording quality is described as good/average but listenable.  Weighted combination yields a rating in the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally well balanced (B+), a little muddy at times, occasional sub‑second dropout on St. Stephen, not the clearest board but fully listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is built around a Lovelight sandwich, leading into a tight Dark Star → St. Stephen → Eleven suite that drives the show’s momentum; transitions are praised and keep the pacing high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia is described as possessed – nonstop, mind‑melting runs on The Eleven and Dark Star, intense focus and creative phrasing throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass is called tight, sparkling and ‘bombing’, especially during the Dark Star and Eleven jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen gets high marks for vocal power on Friend of Mine and Lovelight, with his soulful delivery highlighted as a show‑defining element.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s B3/keyboard is audible (though some note it sounds like a Vox backup), adding texture to the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: A compact drum solo and a unique mid‑set drum break are noted; overall percussion is tight and drives the high energy.
